sections.title: 一、詞彙(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1至10題，每題選出一個最適當的選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/3分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止，未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

sections.title: 四、篇章結構(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第41至45題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (E) 選項中分別選出最適當者，填入空格中，使篇章結構清晰有條理，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/2分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止，未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Many researchers have been interested in whether or not an individual’s birth order has an effect on intelligence. One of the first studies was carried out in the Netherlands during the early 1970s. [[41]] The test was called the “Raven,” which is similar to the I.Q. test. The researchers found a strong relationship between the birth order of the test takers and their scores on the Raven test. [[42]]

In 1975, Zajonc and Markus developed the confluence theory to explain the negative effect of birth order on intelligence involving the data from the Dutch. [[43]] However, Rutherford and Sewell in 1991 tested the theory and found no support for it. They concluded that birth order effects did not exist.

[[44]] On one side there are Zajonc and Markus, who state that birth order effects may be explained solely by family size and the spacing of births. With short birth intervals, increasing order of birth will be associated with lower intelligence levels. But with long birth intervals, this pattern may be reversed. [[45]] They show that the confluence model does not explain any relationship between birth order and intelligence that may exist in the American data. Up to date, there is no agreement between these opposing views. And such a debate may continue for years to come.

options_bank.A: There are definitely two sides to this issue.
options_bank.B: Scores decreased as the family size increased and also with birth order.
options_bank.C: An intelligence test was administered to over 350,000 Dutch males when they turned 19 years of age.
options_bank.D: On the other side are Rutherford and Sewell, who studied more than 10,000 American high school graduates.
options_bank.E: Since then, the theory has been elaborated and even extended to explain the positive effect of birth order on intelligence.

tags.topic: whether birth order affects intelligence: the confluence theory debate

groups.passage:
In recent years, a craze for height has hit hard in industrializing Asian countries like Taiwan, Hong Kong and China, which boast seven of the world’s 10 tallest buildings. The current tallest, at 101 floors, is the Taipei 101 in Taiwan, though Toronto’s CN Tower is 180 feet higher, largely because of its huge antenna. Yet, in the Persian Gulf city of Dubai, the world’s tallest building-to-be is already well under construction. Its pilings are already in place, plunging 160 feet into the earth. When it’s finished, visitors will swoon over this city from 123 stories high, if not more. Currently, however, its exact height is still kept a secret to potential competitors in the world’s race for the title of the tallest skyscraper.

While New York built skyscrapers because land was scarce, Dubai is doing it to get on the world map. “It’s image, clearly,” said Richard Rosan, president of its construction firm. “There’s no practical reason for having a building this tall. You can’t be scared of heights if you want to work on the top floor.”

On paper, the Dubai Tower looks something like a giant space shuttle about to be launched into the clouds. Designers say the silvery steel-and-glass building will restore to the Arab world the honor of hosting the earth’s tallest structure—a title lost in 1889 when the Eiffel Tower upset the 43-century reign of Egypt’s Great Pyramid of Giza.

groups.passage:
Dr. Thompson was pleased. Just three months after moving to the small Midwestern town, he had been invited to address an evening meeting of the Chamber of Commerce. Here was the perfect opportunity to show his knowledge of modern medicine and to get his practice off to a flourishing start. With this in mind, the doctor prepared carefully.

On the night of his speech, Dr. Thompson was delighted to see that the meeting hall was full. After being introduced, he strode confidently to the lectern and announced his topic: “Recent Advances in Medicine.” He began with a detailed discussion of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a rare brain disorder that had recently been covered in the New England Journal of Medicine. Next he outlined the progress that had been made in studying immune system disorders.

Just about this time, halfway through his speech, Dr. Thompson began to notice a certain restlessness in his audience. People were murmuring and shuffling their feet. Someone in the fourth row seemed to be glancing at a newspaper. Nevertheless, Dr. Thompson plowed on. He had saved the best for last. He quoted extensively from an article in the Lancet about genetic research, feeling sure his audience would be impressed by his familiarity with this prestigious British medical journal.

Then the speech was over. Dr. Thompson had expected to be surrounded by enthusiastic people, congratulating him and asking questions. Instead he found himself standing alone. Finally the president of the Chamber of Commerce came up to him. “Something tells me,” said Dr. Thompson, “that my speech was not very successful. I can’t understand it. I worked so hard to make it interesting.” “Oh, it was a fine speech,” replied the president. “But maybe it would have gone over better with a different audience. Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is not exactly a factor in these people’s everyday experience. You know, here we are in January. If you’d talked about ways to avoid getting the flu, you’d have had them on the edge of their seats!”

questions.stem: What is the main message of the passage?

options.A: A good speaker has to be fully prepared regardless of the audience.
options.B: A good speaker should display his learning to the audience in an enthusiastic way.
options.C: The more a speaker wants to please the audience, the more likely he will succeed.
options.D: The key to a successful speech is to make it meaningful and relevant to the audience.

questions.stem: What was the reaction of the audience to Dr. Thompson’s speech?

options.A: They were bored because the medical topics were not their daily concern.
options.B: They did not understand him so they could only discuss among themselves.
options.C: They were impressed by his familiarity with advanced research in medicine.
options.D: They congratulated him on the success of the speech and asked him questions.

questions.stem: Which topic was NOT mentioned in the doctor’s speech?

groups.passage: When a company ventures into new markets, it will need to face various problems. These problems can be broadly classified into several categories, including (1) cultural factors, (2) economic issues, (3) geographical factors, (4) political/legal issues, (5) religious factors, and (6) technological issues. Find an appropriate category for the problems discussed in each of the following paragraphs.

passage_parts.text: A company will face problems of this kind, as it is an alien when compared to the business climate of the country. Coca-Cola, for instance, was faced with such a problem in India, when it was given a choice of either to reveal its secret formula or leave the country. Coke chose to leave. But when it was welcomed back after several years, it was subjected to harassment and constant interference from the political activists.

Problems of this kind can make an impact on the properties of a product. This impact forces a company to adapt its products in order to meet the needs of the local market. To solve the problems, the level of economic development in a market should be assessed, for example, by the level of revenue, buying power of local consumers, and by the state of infrastructure in the foreign market. These indicators can provide vital information to the company regarding its marketing strategy.

These problems are perhaps the biggest issue a researcher can come across while studying new markets. This is because markets that can be classified as similar on various grounds tend to be dissimilar when it comes to this particular aspect. There are differences even within the same country. Accordingly, travel advertising in Canada is divided between the English audience and the French audience. While pictures of travel advertisements show a wife alone for the English audience, a man and wife are shown for the French audience. This is done because the French are more bound by family ties.

sections.title: 二、英文作文(20%)
sections.instructions:
說明：1. 依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。

questions.label: 作文
questions.stem: 提示︰指定科目考試完畢後，高中同學決定召開畢業後的第一次同學會，你被公推負責主辦。請將你打算籌辦的活動寫成一篇短文。文分兩段，第一段詳細介紹同學會的時間、地點及活動內容，第二段則說明採取這種活動方式的理由。

extraction.method: Word 版 paper-2.doc（soffice 轉 docx + python-docx）為主文字來源，選文空格（全形空白包住的題號）改寫為 [[題號]]；以 pdftotext（-layout 與預設模式）擷取 paper-1.pdf，將所有選文、題幹、選項、選項庫依題本順序做英文字詞與標點逐一比對（除空白、題號、頁首頁碼外完全一致），中文說明、翻譯題目、作文提示去除空白後逐字比對一致；以 Read 逐頁檢視題本 PDF 第1–8頁影像確認段落、空格位置與格式（粗體、斜體、外框段落）；答案取自 answer.pdf 第2頁「英文考科選擇題參考答案」（pdftotext，並看頁面影像核對 56 題）；非選擇題評分標準以 pdftotext 擷取 scoring.pdf（選才通訊2005年八月號「94年度指定科目考試非選擇題評分標準說明」，英文在第4–5頁），英文翻譯參考答案（大括號樹狀圖）以 pdftoppm 250 dpi 放大裁切後人工逐格轉寫；統計以 xlrd 讀取 stats-1.xls「英文」工作表與 stats-2.xls 工作表「2」（英文科選擇題選項分析），並以程式核對選項分析標「*」的選項與官方答案一致、其 T／H／L 與 stats-1 的 P／Ph／Pl 一致、D＝Ph－Pl。
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast「94–97」期別一致：詞彙 1–10（10×1，4選項）、綜合測驗 11–30（4篇×5題×1＝20）、文意選填 31–40（選項 (A)–(J) 共10個，10×1）、篇章結構 41–45（選項 (A)–(E) 共5個，5×2）、閱讀測驗 46–56（3篇：46–49、50–53、54–56，4＋4＋3題，11×2＝22）、英文翻譯 2題（題本未印每題配分，每小題4分取自評分標準，共8分）、英文作文 20分（文長至少120個單詞）；第壹部分選擇題 72分、第貳部分非選擇題 28分，合計 100。考試時間 80 分鐘取自封面。本年有倒扣（詞彙／綜合 1/3、文意選填 1/9、篇章結構 1/2、閱讀 2/3），各大題說明已逐字保留。

大題標題照本年題本原文寫成「一、詞彙(10%)」「二、綜合測驗(20%)」…「一、英文翻譯(8%)」「二、英文作文(20%)」（以百分比標示配分、半形括號）。第壹部分原文為「第壹部分：選擇題(佔72分)」、第貳部分為「第貳部分：非選擇題(佔28分)」，part 依 schema 只寫「選擇題」「非選擇題」。說明文字的冒號照題本：詞彙、綜合測驗的說明與作文「提示︰」用 U+FE30（︰），其餘「說明：」用 U+FF1A（：），Word 版與 PDF 文字層一致。本年各大題說明寫「倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止，未作答者，…」（逗號，95 年起改為句號），照原文。英文翻譯、作文說明在題本中為兩行（1.／2.），以換行分隔。各題組前的「第 11 至 15 題為題組」等標題沒有放進 JSON（schema 沒有對應欄位）。
題號重複警告（validator: 題號重複 [1, 2]）是刻意的：英文翻譯在題本中編為 1.、2.，作文沒有題號；validator 要求 no 必須是整數，因此翻譯用 no=1、2（label「翻譯1」「翻譯2」），作文用 no=1（label「作文」），label 皆不重複。做法與 ast-95、ast-97 相同。
詞彙題空格照題本印的底線字元長度保留（第1–4題 4 個、第5–8題 5 個、第9、10題 6 個；Word 與 PDF 一致），未統一長度。閱讀題幹的空格同樣照原文（第47、49題 10 個，第54–56題 6 個）。

Word 版與 PDF 的差異：(1) Word 版第45題空格只有13個全形空白、沒有印題號，PDF 題本（文字層與頁面影像）在該處為「45」，依題本寫成 [[45]]；(2) Word 版第29題空格為「29 」後多一個半形空白，第21–25題組選文 “thieves?  No,” 有兩個空白（PDF 文字層為一個），皆整併為一個空白；(3) Word 版段首的 Tab、選項／選文尾端空白、選項間的 Tab 已去除。
第11–15題組：選文中 Don't、didn't、I've 的撇號在題本（Word 與 PDF 文字層）為直撇 '，其餘 Brown’s、It’s 等為彎撇 ’，照原文保留不統一。

格式未保留：第11–15題組的 The Da Vinci Code.（含句點）、第50–53題組的 New England Journal of Medicine 與 the Lancet 在題本為斜體；第46–49題組選文與第49題題幹的 upset、第50–53題組選文末的 had them on the edge of their seats 與第53題題幹引號內同一片語、第52題題幹的 NOT 在題本為粗體（皆無底線，題目也不是問「畫底線的字」，故不加 <u>）。

第54–56題組：題本先印一段說明文（列出 6 類問題），再依序印三個外框段落，每個段落後各接一題（第54、55、56題，題幹相同皆為 “The most appropriate category for the above paragraph is ______.”）。passage 放說明文，passage_parts 依序放三個外框段落，第1段對應第54題、第2段對應第55題、第3段對應第56題；題本沒有為段落編號或命名，label 與 title 填 null。三題的選項組合不同（第55題為 cultural／economic／geographical／technological），照原文。
中文字形：題本 PDF 頁面影像中「題為題組」「身為地球村」的「為」以「爲」字形顯示，但 PDF 文字層、Word 版與評分標準 PDF 均為「為」，以「為」記錄。
答案檔 answer.pdf 合併國文、英文、數學甲、數學乙、歷史、地理、物理、化學、生物多科，只取第2頁「英文考科選擇題參考答案」56 題。

英文翻譯參考答案在 scoring.pdf 第5頁中是大括號樹狀圖（圖片）。answer 取每個括號的第一個選項、並省略圓括號內的 (,)、(try to) 組成一句（第1題 “As members of the global village, we should not limit ourselves to this small island.”；第2題 “We should not only participate in international activities but also show our own cultural characteristics.”）；accepted_answers 以斜線列出同一位置可替換的字詞並保留圓括號（第1題 limit/confine/restrict；第2題 show/promote、characteristics/features）。本年評分標準未說明圓括號的意義（96 年評分標準註明「( )（括弧）表示該字詞可省略」），此處依慣例解讀為可省略。scoring_notes 另附評分重點、逐格轉寫與評分標準原文，以及編按「文中所列舉的參考答案，只是該題可得滿分的可能情況之一，並非唯一的答案」。

英文作文：官方沒有範文，answer 為 null。本年評分標準說明只有一段概述（內容、組織、句構修辭、用字拼字及標點大小寫；字數過少扣一分、未分段扣一分），沒有像 95 年起的分項式評分指標表，scoring_notes 逐字收錄該段。說明與提示均為「至少120個單詞」「文分兩段」，tags.word_requirement 記為 “at least 120 words”，essay_type 依題目指定兩段內容（第一段時間地點活動、第二段理由）標為 two_paragraph。

統計：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D 取自 stats-1.xls「英文」工作表（報考 116,492、缺考 8,376、到考 108,116 人）；option_rates 取自 stats-2.xls 工作表「2」選項分析的「T」（全體）列，未含「未答」比例，所以各題 option_rates 加總小於 1（未答最高為第24題 27%、第26題 25%、第4題 24%）。stats-1 的五等組 Pa–Pe、D1–D4 與 stats-2 的高／低分組各選項比例（H／L 列）沒有放入（schema 無對應欄位）。

統計交叉核對：56 題選項分析標「*」的選項與官方答案全部一致，D＝Ph－Pl 全部成立；stats-2 標「*」選項的 T／H／L 與 stats-1 的 P／Ph／Pl 只有兩題差 1 個百分點：第9題 T 56% vs P 55%、第34題 T 39% vs P 38% 且 L 16% vs Pl 15%，推測為四捨五入差異。correct_rate／high_group／low_group 以 stats-1 為準，option_rates 照 stats-2 原值（第9題 C＝0.56、第34題 I＝0.39）。
本年只有 stats-1（答對率及鑑別指數）與 stats-2（選擇題選項分析），沒有非選擇題得分分布檔，因此翻譯與作文的 stats 填 null。

標註說明（屬判斷）：第4題 maintenance、第1題 abundant、第5題 circulation、第9題 opposition 以搭配詞（routine maintenance work／an abundant supply／blood circulation／opposition party）記 collocation；第18題 in the future 需由前文 have had（過去）與 may also … affect（未來）的對比判斷，記 discourse；第19、28題分詞構句記 grammar／participle，answer_pos 依其他年度慣例記 verb；第21題 what、第23題 where 記 grammar／relative_clause；第25題 Except for 記 connective／preposition；第33題 uninhabited 需由前句 only 20 are inhabited 推得，記 discourse；第34題 even 修飾比較級 more，記 grammar／comparison；第35題 for 作「因為」解，記 connective／conjunction。篇章結構：第41題以後一句 “The test” 回指 (C) 的 An intelligence test、第42題以 (B) 的 Scores 承接 their scores on the Raven test，皆記 lexical_cohesion；第43題 (E) Since then 承接 1975 年並與後句 However 形成轉折，記 transition_word；第44題 (A) 引出 On one side … 的兩方論點，記 topic_sentence；第45題 (D) On the other side 對應前文 On one side，記 transition_word。閱讀：第46題需由 123 stories vs 101 floors 推算，記 inference；第51題需由聽眾反應與會長的話推論，記 inference；第54–56題要求判斷各段落所屬的問題類別（段落主旨），記 main_idea。題組 sdgs：第16–20題組（技術創新）記 [9]、第21–25題組（文化遺產保護）記 [11]、第31–40題組（澎湖自然保留區、海洋與陸域生態）記 [14, 15]，其餘記 []。
